What is Zapier AI?

AI layer across Zapier's automation platform, which connects 8,000+ apps. Includes natural-language Zap building, AI steps inside workflows, Zapier Agents that act autonomously, Chatbots, Tables, Interfaces and Canvas.

Best for

Connecting the widest possible set of SaaS apps with AI steps in between.

Main features

  • AI Zap builder (describe a workflow in plain language)
  • AI by Zapier steps for extraction, classification and generation inside a Zap
  • Zapier Agents with tool access across all connected apps
  • Chatbots with knowledge sources
  • Tables (database) and Interfaces (forms/apps)
  • Canvas for diagramming processes
  • MCP server exposing Zapier actions to other AI tools.

Practical use cases

  • Routing form submissions into a CRM with AI-extracted fields
  • summarising inbound emails into a Slack digest
  • building an internal chatbot over company documents
  • letting an AI agent triage and respond to routine requests across apps.

Who is it for?

  • Operations, marketing, sales and support teams; non-technical automation builders; small and mid-size businesses.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium; task-metered subscription tiers; agent activity metered separately

Plans described in the source

Free $0 with 100 tasks/month and two-step Zaps only. Professional from roughly $19.99/mo (750 tasks) scaling by task volume. Team from roughly $69/mo with shared workspaces and unlimited users. Enterprise custom, annual. AI features consume tasks; Zapier Agents and Chatbots have their own activity allowances and add-on pricing. Costs scale steeply with task volume - the headline entry price is rarely the real cost.

Free plan

Yes - permanent free plan with 100 tasks/month and single-step Zaps.

Free trial

Yes - 14-day free trial of Professional features on signup.

Usage limits to consider

Task-metered: every step in every Zap run consumes a task, so a 6-step Zap running 100 times uses 600 tasks. AI steps and agent activities consume additional credits. Free tier is limited to 100 tasks and two-step Zaps.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Unmatched app coverage - if a SaaS product exists, Zapier probably connects to it
  • genuinely no-code with a gentle learning curve
  • the MCP server makes Zapier's whole action catalogue available to other AI assistants, which is strategically significant
  • reliable and mature.

Limitations to consider

  • Task-based pricing becomes expensive fast at volume compared with n8n or Make
  • multi-step Zaps consume tasks per step, which surprises new users
  • limited branching and looping logic compared with Make
  • AI steps are convenience wrappers rather than deep capability
  • no self-hosting option.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • Chrome extension
  • mobile app
  • MCP server

Languages

  • Interface in several languages; AI output multilingual

API access

Yes - Zapier Platform API for building integrations; MCP server for AI tool access

Integrations and exports

  • 8,000+ apps - the largest integration catalogue in the category, covering essentially every mainstream SaaS product

Evaluation notes

Calculate cost as (steps x runs), not runs - this is the single most common budgeting error. At high volume, n8n self-hosted or Make will be materially cheaper.
